hermit.name: #given# the hermit
hermit.appearance: {self.Name} sits outside a lean-to of branches, whittling something small.
hermit.description: Wild-haired, barefoot and entirely unbothered by the weather.

profile.motive_text: be left alone with the trees
goals: finish carving a bird that looks like it could fly
profile.backstory: "I lived in the village once. Then I met the forest. The forest was better company."
profile.epilogue: {speaker.The} carves a little wooden figure of you, and sets it on a stump where the birds can see it.

herbalist.name: #given# the herb-wife
herbalist.appearance: {self.Name} is picking through the undergrowth, a basket of leaves on one arm.
herbalist.description: Brisk, sharp-eyed, and smelling powerfully of mint.

profile.motive_text: find a cure for every ill under the sky
goals: find the last ingredient for a remedy nobody has made in a century
profile.backstory: "Somebody has to know which leaf cures and which one kills. It might as well be me."
profile.epilogue: {speaker.The} names a newly found herb after you. It smells awful, but it cures warts.

waystone.name: carved waystone
waystone.appearance: A waystone stands here, its face covered in carving.
waystone.description: Someone has carved a long inscription into its face, letter by careful letter.

journal_page.name: torn journal page
journal_page.description: A page torn from somebody's journal, the ink blurred by rain.

wilds_old_roads.title: The old roads
wilds_old_roads.text: The roads here are older than the kingdoms that claim them. Some say they were laid by people who walked between the stars and the earth.

wilds_forest_rule.title: The forest's rule
wilds_forest_rule.text: Never take more from the forest than you can carry, and never carry more than you can give back.

wilds_lights.title: Marsh lights
wilds_lights.text: The lights over the marsh are the souls of travellers who took the wrong path. Follow them, and you will join them.

wilds_standing_stones.title: The standing stones
wilds_standing_stones.text: The spiral stones were raised to remember something. Nobody remembers what. The stones, presumably, do.
